summary: Cold read of the recorded assistant-bounded-generation contract and task plan returned NOT CONVERGED with nine findings. All were verified against the repository and all held; four would have shipped bugs. The contract promised a typed backend_error the port cannot express, scoped a retry on a predicate that conflates an absent tool block with a malformed one, specified a second attempt identical to the first under temperature 0, and named request.on('close') as the disconnect signal although Node emits it on normal completion. Required leaves rose from six to eight and write_scope from fifteen to seventeen paths.

criteria_map.The selector Converse request carries ma: The cap. Verified: bedrock.provider.ts:394 sends only { temperature: 0, topP: 1 }. The criterion now requires the assertion on the REQUEST OBJECT, because a timing test passes without the fix - the uncapped call is fast when there is no prior turn.
criteria_map.A selector response with NO TOOL BLOCK i: The retry, which the read showed was not expressible and not safe. LlmSelectionOutcome (llm.interface.ts:27) is selection | clarify | unsupported with no backend-error arm, and chat.service.ts:177 treats anything else AS A SELECTION, so the promised typed backend_error could not be returned; bedrock.provider.ts:231 tests !toolUse?.name, which is true for an absent block AND a present malformed one, so the retry could fire on malformed input; and an identical capped temperature-zero second attempt would reproduce the same result. All three are now in the criterion, with attempt two raising the cap and skipped after cancellation.
criteria_map.The request is bounded as SERVER RESOURC: The request bound, restated as resource safety with a named measured representation - JSON.stringify(priorTurns) at ingress, before the trim and before prompt construction - and with the limits exported from @3f/contract so the client can trim to the same contract; otherwise the ninth ask becomes a 400. Retention and oldest-first order are unchanged because chat.service.ts:153 reads at(-1) as the latest turn.
criteria_map.Server-side cancellation is wired and is: Cancellation, corrected on three points the read found: request.on('close') is the wrong signal because Node emits IncomingMessage close on normal completion; the abort must be passed to send(), which bedrock.provider.ts:382 calls with no options today, or a fake false-greens the proof; and the abort must be checked immediately before warehouse.execute(), since SelectionExecutor.run awaits explain() first. The bounded limit - an in-flight query expires under statement_timeout - is the human's decision and is written at the seam.
criteria_map.The behaviour is proven by hermetic leav: The proof, which grew from six leaves to eight: a no_tool_block followed by mark_unsupported or clarify must return THAT outcome rather than mask it, and a normal completion must NOT abort while a premature close must. D-0006 was corrected from one file to FOUR - bedrock.provider.ts, llm.constants.ts, mock.provider.ts and chat.constants.ts are all ignored and baseline-pinned.

current_flow: The assistant is shipped and correct but a follow-up question can take 39 to 214 seconds, because bedrock.provider.ts:394 builds the only inferenceConfig with temperature and topP and no maxTokens. Nothing else in the path is at fault: the prompt is small and constant, toolChoice is already forced, and the same call with no prior turn returns in about a second. Cancellation does not exist: the stream controller writes frames and ends in a finally block without observing disconnect, and no abort signal reaches the model or the executor.
new_abstractions: Two new outcomes on the LlmProvider port - a no_tool_block discriminant and a backend-error arm - which is the first time this port can report that the model returned nothing usable as distinct from refusing.
An AbortSignal threaded from the HTTP boundary through the provider to the AWS transport and to the executor seam, the first cancellation path in this codebase.
Ingress limits shared through @3f/contract so a server bound and a client trim can be the same number rather than two numbers that drift.
gaps: The contract promised a typed backend_error outcome the port cannot express: LlmSelectionOutcome (llm.interface.ts:27) is selection | clarify | unsupported, and chat.service.ts:177 treats every non-clarify, non-unsupported result as a selection, so throwing would produce a buffered HTTP envelope rather than the promised typed AskResponse.

'No tool block' was ambiguous: bedrock.provider.ts:231 tests !toolUse?.name, which is true both for an absent block and for a present block with no name, so a malformed input could be retried - the case the contract explicitly forbids. The proof also omitted the no_tool_block followed by mark_unsupported or clarify sequence, the one most likely to mask a genuine refusal.

The retry's second request was unspecified and, as implied, a no-op: repeating an identical capped temperature-zero request reproduces the same tool-less result rather than recovering it, and nothing prohibited a second attempt after cancellation had arrived.

The cancellation proof could false-green: bedrock.provider.ts:382 calls send(command) with no options, so a controller fake that merely receives a signal does not prove the abort reaches the AWS transport; and an abort arriving after selection could still START a query, since only already-running queries are meant to finish.

D-0006 coverage was incomplete: besides bedrock.provider.ts, the scoped llm.constants.ts, mock.provider.ts and chat.constants.ts are also prettier-ignored and baseline-pinned, so editing any of them without the same de-ignore and hash-removal ritual fails the quality gate.

Two manual verification steps were impossible as written: latency_ms and output_tokens are audit_events row fields rather than backend log fields, and enforcing a serialized-size limit requires naming the representation that is measured.
contradictions: The approved plan has five task leaves and assigns server-side cancellation to its task 2, while the recorded decomposition has the three the human chose after approval and assigns cancellation to this task; ownership, dependencies and Surface Impact cannot all be true at once.
The confirmed spec required cancellation to reach the query work while the human had settled on bounded cancellation, in which an in-flight query expires under statement_timeout.

request.on('close') was named as the disconnect signal, but Node emits IncomingMessage's close on normal request completion, so the listener would abort healthy SSE requests and could miss genuine abandonment.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-abg-c2 adds BOTH a no_tool_block outcome and a backend-error outcome to the port, handled explicitly by chat.service, so the promised typed answer is representable rather than thrown.

REPO-ANSWERED - the mapper must distinguish an undefined tool block from a present-but-malformed one before any retry decision, and a required leaf now covers no_tool_block followed by mark_unsupported or clarify returning that outcome rather than masking it.
REPO-ANSWERED - the second attempt RAISES the cap so it differs from the first, and is not made at all if cancellation has arrived.

REPO-ANSWERED - the AbortSignal must be passed to send() rather than merely accepted by the provider, and is also checked immediately before warehouse.execute(), since SelectionExecutor.run awaits warehouse.explain() first; a required leaf proves a normal completion does NOT abort while a premature close does.
REPO-ANSWERED - the disconnect signal is a premature response/socket close, not request.on('close').
REPO-ANSWERED - D-0006 is restated as FOUR files, each formatted, de-ignored and removed from the quality-gate baseline map in the same change.
REPO-ANSWERED - the manual check reads audit_events rather than the backend log, and the measured representation for the size limit is named as JSON.stringify(priorTurns) at ingress.
HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the confirmed spec was amended and re-confirmed to the settled bounded-cancellation decision rather than leaving the contradiction as a recorded supersession.

ORCHESTRATOR-RECORDED - the plan-versus-decomposition contradiction is resolved in favour of the DECOMPOSITION, because the human chose three tasks after the plan was approved and the plan body is digest-locked. reviewer_focus names it first so a reviewer does not reject this task's scope on the plan's wording.

The approved plan's Task Decomposition section still lists five leaves and cannot be edited without invalidating its approval digest.

rounds.question: Closing the task grill for `assistant-bounded-generation`. All nine findings verified and folded in — four would have shipped bugs. The port literally couldn't express the contract (`LlmSelectionOutcome` has no backend-error arm, and `chat.service.ts:177` treats anything that isn't clarify/unsupported as a *selection*), `!toolUse?.name` conflates an **absent** tool block with a **malformed** one so the retry could fire on exactly the case it must not, the retry as specified was a **no-op** (temperature 0, so repeating an identical capped request reproduces the same result — attempt two now raises the cap), and `request.on("close")` would have aborted **healthy** SSE requests because Node emits it on normal completion too. Also corrected: the abort must reach `send()` (the real seam passes no options, so a fake would false-green), a query must not *start* after an abort (`explain()` is awaited before `execute()`), D-0006 covers **four** prettier-ignored files rather than one, and two of my manual checks were impossible — `latency_ms`/`output_tokens` live in `audit_events`, not the log. Required leaves 6→8, scope 15→17 paths.
